title: Can I BEAT YouTube Chess?
summary: The creator plays the chess game in YouTube Playables (YouTube's built-in mini-games). It has six AI levels shown as an avatar whose brain grows bigger inside its head from level 1 to level 6. Colour is picked at random. Goal: beat every level; he beats all six in turn (level 1 in 1:49), commenting that the bots make 'programmed' beginner errors such as moving a piece twice in the opening or developing a bishop behind a pawn, and that the top level still gives up (e.g. Qf7 'equivalent of resigning'). Ends by comparing it to in-flight seatback chess.
rules: Six AI levels played in order 1 -> 6; colour randomly assigned each game (he chooses 'random').
Player can only highlight pieces, not squares (UI limitation noted at 0:51).
Undo and settings buttons exist in the side panel (frame observation).
win_condition: Checkmate (or bot gives up) each of the 6 levels; beat level 6 to complete.

opponent.name: YouTube Playables Chess AI, Levels 1-6
opponent.avatar_description: Cartoon head avatar with a visible brain that grows from teeny-tiny (level 1) to filling most of the head (level 6). Remake: simple round head outline with a pink brain blob scaled by level.

board.theme_notes: Warm wooden board with wooden side panels holding captured-piece trays, undo and settings icons (YouTube Playables look).

events: Level ladder: after each win advance to next brain level; levels roughly 'beginner-ish' throughout with occasional positional errors.
visual_fx: Level-select screen with six brain-size avatars.
Wood-texture UI chrome; captured pieces stacked in side trays.
